questions.title: Which two countries will reach the final of the 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations?
questions.background: The Women's Africa Cup of Nations is Africa's continental championship for women's national football teams. The winners of its two semifinals advance to the final.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : CAF's official tournament results, supported where necessary by contemporaneous match reporting. Resolution : Resolve once both semifinals of the 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations have concluded and the two finalists have been determined. The result of the final itself is not relevant. Accepted Answer Format : The two finalist country names in alphabetical order, separated by a comma.

Separately, Cameroon (6 pts) are mathematically 100% locked into D1 (Half 1) via CAF H2H wins over both Mali (2-1) and Ghana (1-0). Removing the ~15% Group A placement uncertainty in our 4-model bracket Monte Carlo (160,000 sims with exact CAF H2H tiebreakers) boosts Morocco-side pairings and specifically elevates Algeria, Morocco from ~0.07 outside into the top 5 at 0.08 (replacing Ghana, Nigeria at ~0.075, since Ghana still face ~30-33% group-stage elimination vs Mali on Aug 6 while Algeria are 100% guaranteed a Half 2 QF2 vs weak Group B winner Ivory Coast/Tanzania/Burkina Faso). questions.title: Which DRC province will WHO identify as experiencing a surge in weekly Ebola cases in mid-September 2026?
questions.background: The Democratic Republic of Congo declared an Ebola outbreak in May 2026.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : WHO public statements about the DRC Ebola outbreak, including statements quoted in contemporaneous reputable news reporting. Resolution Window : Resolve to the province explicitly identified by WHO as experiencing surging weekly Ebola cases in its outbreak assessment publicly reported between September 10 and September 16, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the province.
questions.current_reasoning: Hard provincial data from DRC INSP SitRep 073 (published July 27, data to July 26: 3,262 cases, 1,437 deaths) alongside July 30 Al Jazeera/AP updates (3,442 confirmed cases, 1,521 deaths—a 50% one-week death spike with 50 deaths in 24 hours; Uganda declared Ebola-free July 28): (1) North Kivu overtakes Ituri for #1 (0.29 -> 0.35) after reaching 314 confirmed cases and 204 deaths, with Ebola treatment center bed occupancy jumping from 120% (July 21) to 136.2% (192 patients for 141 beds) plus 11 infected health workers—signaling an accelerating secondary wave in Katwa/Butembo/M23-affected corridors well positioned for a mid-September WHO weekly surge call. (2) Ituri remains strong at #2 (0.32 -> 0.31) with 2,901 cases (88.9% of total) and 1,207 deaths amid July 28 Bunia health worker strikes, the Nyakunde facility attack, and 60.9% community deaths. (3) Haut-Uele rises to #3 (0.13 -> 0.15) with 38 confirmed cases and formal inclusion in the expanded four-province UN Ebola response appeal. (4) Tshopo drops sharply to #4 (0.19 -> 0.12) after holding flat at 5 confirmed cases with zero new cases from July 21 to July 26, confirming containment of Kisangani's imported cluster so far while retaining river-corridor re-introduction risk. (5) South Kivu stays at 0.02 (3 cumulative cases, 61 consecutive days with zero new cases; 5% residual for Bas-Uele/Maniema/Kinshasa).

questions.current_reasoning: Florida candidate qualifying closed June 12 with four Republicans on the August 18 FL-7 ballot: incumbent Cory Mills, former FOX 35 Orlando news anchor Ryan Elijah, Port Orange business owner Sarah Ulrich, and 2024 primary foe Michael Don Johnson. questions.title: To which hospital will Pakistan’s Supreme Court order Imran Khan transferred for medical care in August 2026?
questions.background: Former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan is imprisoned at Adiala jail. His eye condition has required specialist treatment, and concerns about his health have been central to his party’s campaign for his release.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The Supreme Court’s order or contemporaneous reporting by established news organizations describing its requirements. Resolution : Resolve to the hospital designated in the Supreme Court’s next order, issued after the start date and during August 2026, directing Khan’s transfer from Adiala jail for hospital care. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the hospital.
questions.current_reasoning: Imran Khan and his sister Uzma Khan filed pending Supreme Court appeals in May 2026 (most recently May 19) specifically requesting his transfer from Adiala Jail to Islamabad's Shifa International Hospital for right central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) and blood-clot monitoring, making Shifa International Hospital the leading candidate if the court grants transfer relief. However, authorities have taken him to Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) for all five intravitreal injections in 2026 (most recently June 14-15), making a court-ordered inpatient transfer to PIMS a strong government-acceptable compromise. Prof. Dr. Nadeem Qureshi of Rawalpindi's Al-Shifa Trust Eye Hospital already sits on the court-mandated medical board, making it the clear specialist third option, with smaller tail probabilities on AFIO and Shaukat Khanum.

local_articles.title: Supreme Court Deals Trump Final Humiliation After He Missed Deadline
local_articles.snippet: The Supreme Court has put a decisive end to one of President Donald Trump’s signature crusades after he missed the deadline to seek a rehearing. When the court struck down Trump’s bid to end birthright citizenship for millions of Americans in a 6-3 ruling at the end of June, it started a 25-day clock for the president to seek a reversal of the decision, which he vowed to do. But that deadline came and went without the Trump administration submitting such a filing. Now, the Supreme Court has put the final nail in the coffin, issuing a certified judgment and affirming a lower court ruling that had blocked the president’s executive order seeking to ban automatic citizenship to children born on U.S. soil to parents in the country temporarily or illegally. local_articles.title: "Bar Councils Have Become Men's Clubs": Supreme Court Says Co-Opt Women Members
local_articles.snippet: New Delhi: Observing that State Bar Councils have increasingly become "men's clubs", the Supreme Court on Tuesday directed the Chief Justices of the jurisdictional High Courts to nominate two co-opted women members to each State Bar Council. The top court said the two women members co-opted shall be nominated from among former women High Court judges or senior women members of the Bar. The top court, in December 2023, had ordered that 30 per cent representation in State Bar Councils be provided to women lawyers. To address contingencies where an insufficient number of women is elected, the bench had allowed for a "co-option" mechanism to fill up to 10 per cent of those seats. local_articles.title: Why Imran Khan Returned To Acting After 10 Years With Adhure Hum Adhure Tum
local_articles.snippet: New Delhi: Actor Imran Khan is returning to the big screen after a decade with Netflix's upcoming romantic comedy Adhure Hum Adhure Tum. The actor, last seen on screen in Nikkhil Advani's 2015 film Katti Batti, also starring Kangana Ranaut, will next be seen in a new-age love story. In a recent conversation with The Hollywood Reporter India, Imran confirmed that he has finished shooting the film, adding Adhure Hum Adhure Tum is his first movie in 10 years and will release on Netflix by the end of this year. Imran said it is a "grown-up romantic comedy" that matches where he is in life today. "It's for Netflix and is scheduled to come out at the end of this year. It's a grown-up romantic comedy... age-appropriate to where I am now," he said. The actor also revealed that he worked with young actor Gurfateh Pirzada in the film.
